title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page is a handwritten note on the verso of a typescript sheet from SGA 7, Exposé IX (Néron models and monodromy, §12–13). That typescript is unrelated scrap paper. The mathematics belongs to the 1976 IHÉS lecture on divided-power (p.d.) de Rham complexes.

(1) Morphisms of models. A morphism u: Â** → Â'** is considered between completed bigraded p.d. algebras. Each completion is the product ∏_i A_i (resp. ∏_j A'_j) of its graded pieces. u is a ring homomorphism ∏A_i → ∏A'_j that:
- sends the augmentation ideal Â**+ into Â'**+,
- is compatible with the divided powers,
- satisfies u(T) = T for a distinguished element T.
A priori u only induces a p.d.-compatible map k{T} → k{T} on cohomology. Here k{T} (divided-power algebra on T) is identified with H*(A**) and H*(A'**). The condition u(T) = T rigidifies the morphisms, a kind of normalisation or orientation on a canonical cohomology class.

(2) Groupoids of models. For the categories DRsp(X,k), DRsp'(X,k), DRsp unifl(X,k), DRsp unifl'(X,k), he forms the associated groupoids (subscript 0): the groupoid obtained by formally inverting all arrows. These are p.d. de Rham-type models of X over k; 'sp' and 'unifl' are unidentified qualifiers on the models, possibly 'spécial' and 'uniformément ...', which cannot be read with certainty. He writes a commutative square of functors:
- Horizontal maps C → C_0 are surjective on objects.
- The vertical maps (forgetful or primed variants) are essentially surjective, and on the 'unifl' side also fully faithful.
- Some C_0 are noted equivalent to full subcategories, conditionally ("si unifl. stable par T_i").

(3) Conclusion. Chasing the diagram shows that DRsp'(X,k)_0 and DRsp unifl'(X,k)_0 are 'pointed groupoids': connected groupoids with a family of objects on which the morphisms act transitively. So they are equivalent to the automorphism group of any one object. The page breaks off at "Donc ils sont con[nexes / équivalents]".

The purpose is the standard uniqueness-of-model statement: any two p.d. de Rham models of X are linked by a zig-zag. The associated groupoid is connected, so the model is unique up to non-canonical isomorphism, with an automorphism group as the remaining invariant. This is the analogue, over a general ring k with divided powers, of the uniqueness of Sullivan minimal models up to (homotopy) isomorphism.
errors: The argument is sketched, not proved: the essential surjectivity and full faithfulness of the vertical functors are asserted without proof.
The identification H*(A**) ≅ k{T} presupposes a specific X whose cohomology is a divided-power algebra on one generator; this cannot be checked from the page.

Concluding connectedness of the groupoids from functors that are only 'surjective on objects' plus essential surjectivity needs an extra argument. One must show that any two objects are linked by a zig-zag, which requires something like a common refinement; this is not written out.

ideas.what: Rigidified morphisms of completed p.d. models: ring maps compatible with divided powers, preserving augmentation ideals and fixing a distinguished generator T
ideas.modern_name: Morphisms of augmented complete divided-power (bi)graded algebras / p.d. cdga models
ideas.usually_credited_to: Divided powers: H. Cartan (1950s); p.d. de Rham complexes: Berthelot, Illusie
ideas.where_published: Only in the unpublished 1976 IHÉS lecture notes (this dossier)

ideas.what: Passing from a category of models to its associated groupoid (inverting all arrows) and showing it is connected (a 'pointed groupoid')
ideas.modern_name: Groupoid localization / uniqueness of minimal models up to homotopy; classifying space of models connected
ideas.usually_credited_to: Sullivan (1977) for minimal models; Gabriel–Zisman (1967) for localization
ideas.where_published: Similar groupoid-of-models reasoning appears in Pursuing Stacks (1983), but not this specific statement

ideas.what: Comparison of model categories with and without the 'unifl' condition via commutative squares of functors, with stability under T_i as a condition
ideas.modern_name: Equivalence of subcategories of cofibrant/minimal models after localization

missed.claim: The page is a fragment of Grothendieck's unpublished 1976 programme of divided-power de Rham models of homotopy types over arbitrary rings k, a p.d. analogue of Sullivan theory. It includes the step that the groupoid of such models is connected, so models are unique up to non-canonical isomorphism. Later work on algebraic models of p-adic and integral homotopy uses E∞-algebras instead (Mandell; Toën's 'schématisation'). The divided-power route is rarely credited to Grothendieck in detail.
missed.quote: qui montre que les deux catégories déduites DRsp'(X,k)_0 et DRsp unifl'(X,k)_0 sont des groupoïdes ponctuels
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical evidence for an alternative, divided-power approach to integral algebraic models of homotopy types. That approach is of interest relative to recent work on p.d./cosimplicial algebra models and derived de Rham theory. The page itself contains only a routine uniqueness step.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine technical step: rigidified morphisms and a uniqueness-of-model argument via groupoid localization, within an unpublished but known project. It contains no unexpected result; its interest lies mainly in documenting the divided-power homotopy-model programme of 1976.
transcription_corrections: Line 2: the products ∏A_i and ∏A'_j are written under Â** and Â'** with '‖' (equality signs), meaning Â** = ∏ A_i (product of graded pieces).
'hom d'anneaux de ∏A_i dans ∏A'_j qui induit Â**+ dans Â'**+ et compatible aux p.d., et tel que u(T)=T': the word after 'u(T)=T' looks like 'où' or 'OK', not 'cas'.
'a priori u: k{T} → k{T}, hom[omorphisme]': the cohomology isomorphisms are ≅ H*(A**) and ≅ H*(A'**).

Diagram labels: top horizontal 'surj. sur ob. pl.' may read 'surj. sur ob. [et] pl[einement fidèle]'. The first vertical arrow reads 'ess. surjectif, sur obj.' and the lower one 'ess. surjectif, pleinement fidèle' (partly struck/unclear).
The right-hand vertical arrows are curved ones marking the induced functors between the _0 groupoids.
End: 'des groupoïdes ens[emblistes?] ponctuels (i.e. munis d'une famille d'objets ayant ensemble transitif ...)'. The final word likely begins 'con[nexes]'.
